_comment: Owner waiver, not a legal review. Jayden (repo owner) elected on 2026-07-27 not to conduct a formal GPL-3.0 determination for this personal-scale research run. The answers below record that decision honestly; they do not claim a review took place. If this artifact is ever distributed, served, published, or made commercial, this file must be replaced by an actual determination first.

sources.name: junwang4/causal-language-use-in-science
sources.licence: GPL-3.0 on the repository. No separate data-licence statement exists upstream; the README's 'About the data' section is only a label legend, and 'How to cite' is an academic norm rather than a licence term.

gpl3_determination._comment: Recorded as a waiver by the repo owner. No lawyer was consulted and no formal review was performed.
gpl3_determination.determined_by: uandiqueue (repo owner) — self-assessed, no formal review
gpl3_determination.covers_annotations_as_data: Not determined. GPL-3.0 sits on a repository containing both code (main.py) and data, with no separate data-licence statement, so whether it reaches the annotations is ambiguous. Left unresolved deliberately: the run stays inside the non-distribution boundary where the question does not need an answer.
gpl3_determination.weights_are_derivative_work: Not determined; the question is legally unsettled and actively litigated. No position is asserted in either direction. The run does not rely on this resolving favourably.
gpl3_determination.accepts_obligations_for_non_distributed_: Yes. GPL-3.0 s2 permits making, running and propagating covered works that are not conveyed, without conditions, and s0 excludes mere network interaction from 'conveying'. This artifact is trained locally, is non-serving, and is never distributed, so the source-disclosure obligations in s5/s6 are not triggered regardless of how the two questions above would resolve.
gpl3_determination.may_move_to_served_or_commercial_context: No. Any serving, publication of weights, shipping inside an application, or commercial use requires a fresh determination first, and most likely retraining from a differently-licensed corpus. Note that distributing the weights WOULD be conveying even though network serving alone would not.

approved_uses: local, non-commercial research pilot (viceroy-causal-language-risk-v0) — non-serving, no production traffic, artifact never distributed or published
NOT approved: serving, publishing or shipping the weights, redistribution of the corpus, commercial use, or merging these weights or this data with any other model in the roster
risk_containment: weights, code, and release prefix stay in a namespace separate from every other model in the roster — no shared checkpoints, no merged artifacts, no joint release manifest
the release manifest names the GPL-3.0 dependency explicitly
the corpus and any trained weights stay out of git (see this bundle's .gitignore)
notes: The upstream sentences are verbatim excerpts from PubMed abstracts, i.e. third-party copyrighted material the corpus authors redistributed themselves. That is a further reason to keep the artifact undistributed, independent of the GPL-3.0 question.
